title: The Market Taketh and the Market Giveth Back
summary: Cboe Global Markets, a leading provider of market infrastructure and tradable products, delivers cutting-edge trading, clearing and investment solutions to market participants around the world.
body_markdown:
*JJ Kinahan is Senior Vice President, Head of Retail Expansion and Alternative Investment Products at Cboe Global Markets, Inc. (Cboe).*


**Key Takeaways:**


- **Huang’s return to Nvidia sets market on fire**
- **Investors question whether Huang is too big to fire**
- **Anthropic gets little attention in options pit**


Talk about whiplash. Monday’s market roared higher after Nvidia announced Jensen Huang was back at the helm, underscoring just how quickly investor sentiment can shift from melancholy to merriment on a single headline.


After a wildly dramatic week of heavy selling and growing doubts about the costs and sustainability of artificial intelligence (AI), not to mention Nvidia itself, investors seemed to react with madcap joy, sending Nvidia shares and the shares of other AI-focused companies soaring. The three major indices grabbed back a chunk of last week’s losses.


Cboe Volatility Index® (the VIX® Index) also welcomed the rally, falling by nearly 26% to 26.62. While that might be considered a sign of relief, it is still in warning territory, but not the red flag of danger territory it was approaching last week.


Monday’s rally was a striking reminder that investor sentiment can sometimes trump fundamentals, corporate outlooks and even longer-term concerns about an industry. The upswing appeared extraordinary in both magnitude and its apparent dependence on the comings and goings of one man. The market reaction seemed to put confidence back into the AI trade – maybe not to the levels we’ve seen much of the past year – and underscored how powerful Huang is as one of the faces of AI.


It also may raise the bigger question asked by market and political commentators: Has Nvidia become too big to fail or has Huang become too big to fire?


Nvidia shares led the charge that helped the three major indices recover much of last week’s losses, lifting the S&P 500 Index and the Dow Jones Industrial Average out of correction territory. The Nasdaq Composite, however, is still in a correction, sitting 13% below its October peak.


Nvidia shares closed nearly 31.5% higher, their best showing since 2003, adding nearly $1 trillion back to its market capitalization. The technology-laden Nasdaq Composite advanced 6.5% and the Nasdaq 100 Index gained 6.7%. The Dow reclaimed 3% and the S&P 500 recaptured everything it lost on Friday alone and then some, with a 4.7% gain that settled the index at 7,237.


In the options market, Nvidia appeared to steal Anthropic’s thunder on its first day of trading. Nvidia options volume ran at roughly three times its normal level. That may have left less room for Anthropic to grab the spotlight on its options trading debut.


Still, Anthropic was not totally ignored. Its options are already pricing in a potential $19 implied move in shares between now and the Dec. 18 expiration — a big swing that points to the volatility surrounding the newly public AI company.


Elsewhere, Crowdstrike apparently failed to satisfy investors with its $43.9 billion pact to purchase Zscaler, a deal that would create the world’s largest cybersecurity firm. Crowdstrike’s shares fell nearly 9% while Zscaler’s rose nearly 18%, though below the implied acquisition price of $260.41 per share. Commentators noted that the all-stock deal will include issuing new shares and could meaningfully dilute shareholder value.
